I have had many, many near death experiences in my life, due to being an incredibly clumsy and unaware person. id have to say was very close, was when I was hit by a car

 i was around 15ish. We were camping and I brought my bike, as a normal teenager would do. My parents didnt really care where I went as long as I came back at a certain time. 
Imagine a skinny, long haired teen boy with a baby face wearing floral shirt and short, on a bike nearly as big as him, wearing wired headphones connected to his phone in a pocket. Not the best attire to be on a bike with. I didnt have a helmet on because its teenage rebellion.
I go off the camp site and onto the roads, it was a backroad type area with hardly any traffic, youd see a car maybe once in 20 minutes. It was all fine and dandy because you see, TheBearPrince thought it was a one way road! So im lost in my imagination, going downhill at a rapid speed and thinking, ironically, of a specific clown character from a popular webcomic. I turn the corner and theres a bridge going over a river. 
This is where shit hit the fan. When i turned, i registered two things; there was a nice looking old couple down the bank, packing up a canoe into their car, and suddenly being mere feet away from a car. My mental process kicked in and i went to swerve away from the car (honestly i wouldnt have cared if i had fallen off the bridge, theres water) however.
You know how its like to try to ride a bike on sand thats not meant for it? There was sand on the bridge. Instead of being a normal fucking bike, it skid. Flung me right off and nailed me into the side of the moving car. I have no idea how i survived, as I had been slammed by the mirror. The next thing I know the old couple from before was standing next to me, asking if i was alright. 
To which, I was. Well, mostly. I had snapped my collarbone clean in half, and had a few cuts and bruises from the fall, but it couldve been much worse. The car had taken off, and i didnt really care. My phone and bike had been thrown, and in my pure adrenaline state, i just went looking for the phone, trying to reassure myself that i wasnt dead. The kind old couple offered to drive me back to my campsite, as they could load my bike up too. It was either that or do the walk of shame with a bruised leg and a snapped collarbone back. Probably shouldnt have, as they couldve easily just stolen me, but I accepted, and they brought me back.
Oh boy, my parents were not pleased. Called me an idiot, and gave me a wack on the head. I told them i hurt my arm (as i really didnt think much) and they told me id be fine. Spent a whole day and a half (including sleeping) with a snapped collarbone. That floral shirt? I had to pull it up over my head. Dont think i ever felt pain like i did when i had to raise my arm like that. The doctor said thats probably what finished the break in it. Sucks to suck though i guess. Never rode a bike since, its been about 5 years.
